record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.original_question: Find a useful generalization of the inequality tr(exp(A)exp(A^T)) <= tr(exp(A + A^T)) that remains informative for large time in stability problems by incorporating a Lyapunov weighting term of the form exp(A^T P + P A), where P is positive definite and chosen so that A^T P + P A is negative definite. The source proposes this as a way to avoid the conservatism of the naive bound as t tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Hence if A is stable, then the left-hand side of (3.16) will converge to zero, whereas the right-hand side may be unbounded, rendering the bound useless.

To resolve the possible conservatism in (3.16) for t -> infinity, it is natural to conjecture generalizations of (3.14) to include terms of the form e^{A^T P + P A}, where the positive definite matrix P is chosen as in Lyapunov stability theory to render A^T P + P A negative definite.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real square matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n	imes n}$, the Golden–Thompson type inequality
$$\operatorname{tr} igl(e^{A} e^{A^{T}} igr) \;\le\; \operatorname{tr} igl(e^{A+A^{T}} igr)$$
holds. If one replaces $A$ by $tA$ for $t \ge 0$ and $A$ is Hurwitz stable (i.e. every eigenvalue of $A$ has negative real part), then the left-hand side $\operatorname{tr}(e^{tA} e^{tA^{T}})$ tends to $0$ as $t 	o \infty$, while the right-hand side $\operatorname{tr}(e^{t(A+A^{T})})$ may grow unboundedly (since $A+A^{T}$ need not be negative definite even when $A$ is stable). Hence the bound becomes uninformative for large $t$.

Given a Hurwitz stable $A$, by Lyapunov's theorem there exists a positive definite symmetric matrix $P \succ 0$ such that $A^{T}P + PA \prec 0$.

Problem: Find a useful generalization of the inequality $\operatorname{tr}(e^{A} e^{A^{T}}) \le \operatorname{tr}(e^{A+A^{T}})$ that incorporates a Lyapunov weighting term of the form $e^{A^{T}P + PA}$ (with $P \succ 0$ chosen so that $A^{T}P + PA \prec 0$), in such a way that the resulting inequality remains nontrivial and informative as $t 	o \infty$ when $A$ is replaced by $tA$. Concretely, identify and prove a trace inequality involving $e^{tA}$, $e^{tA^{T}}$, $P$, and $e^{t(A^{T}P+PA)}$ (or related Lyapunov-weighted matrix exponentials) that yields a finite, non-conservative bound on $\operatorname{tr}(e^{tA} e^{tA^{T}})$ uniformly in $t \ge 0$.
